scope: Three complete annual topic chapters, all original/current overviews and fifteen sections/paragraphs, and the identity, attribution, date, limitations and substantive notes of thirteen inherited source profiles. No external source, regulatory update, PDF, model experiment, factory observation or farm dataset was newly inspected.

records.reviewer_kind: AI editorial assessment authorized by user
records.rationale: Accept with one attribution clarification: explicitly identify MEP results as client-reported estimates rather than audited firm accounts. The chapter otherwise consistently separates program membership, factory populations, qualified output and proposed evidence fields.

readings.title: Advanced Manufacturing: from a demonstrated process to dependable production

reviewed_section_hashes.heading: Read institutions and statistics at their intended scale
Workforce and facilities need a joined chronology
What a stronger next edition would add

required_presentation_changes.prior: NIST's manufacturing office and the Manufacturing USA directory identify programs, institutes and research networks. They help locate people, facilities and projects, but membership is not a production credential. MEP network results add reported business effects, with attribution to participating clients. Those results should retain their survey basis and separate sales, savings, investment and employment. Census establishment data offers a different statistical perspective; the ASM-to-AIES transition requires a documented bridge before a reader treats successive releases as a continuous manufacturing trend.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: NIST's manufacturing office and the Manufacturing USA directory identify programs, institutes and research networks. They help locate people, facilities and projects, but membership is not a production credential. The retained MEP network-results profile identifies client-reported estimates rather than audited firm accounts. Those results should keep their survey basis and separate sales, savings, investment and employment instead of combining unlike units into one score. Census establishment data offers a different statistical perspective; the ASM-to-AIES transition requires a documented bridge before successive releases can be treated as a continuous manufacturing trend.

claim_findings.rationale: Retain line, establishment, company and region as different populations. The bottleneck, price and acquisition examples describe possible alternative explanations, not newly observed facts or firm-specific causes.

claim_findings.section_heading: Read institutions and statistics at their intended scale
claim_findings.rationale: Qualify MEP survey attribution explicitly as client-reported estimates, not audited firm accounts. Retain separate sales, savings, investment and employment units, directory-versus-production boundaries and the required ASM-to-AIES comparability bridge.

Retain process revision, lot, yield, rework, scrap, customer acceptance, product mix and downtime as proposed reporting fields. The chapter supplies no measured factory observations or universal production metric.

claim_findings.section_heading: Workforce and facilities need a joined chronology
claim_findings.rationale: Retain distinct training enrollment, completion, credential, placement and retention cohorts. Training delivery is not proof that a particular employer filled vacancies, and equipment installation is not qualified production readiness.

claim_findings.section_heading: What a stronger next edition would add
claim_findings.rationale: Retain same-establishment later periods, consistent definitions and alternative explanations before sustained or broader economic claims. No company ranking or causal manufacturing outcome is admitted.

records.reviewer_kind: AI editorial assessment authorized by user
records.rationale: Accept with one scope clarification: explicitly retain the separate food and feed decision boundaries in the inherited CFIA profile and avoid implying that this editorial assessment verifies current legal authority. Research, forecasts and producer outcomes remain properly distinguished.

readings.title: Agriculture and Bioeconomy: following research into fields and livelihoods

reviewed_section_hashes.heading: Separate a research program from a field result
Regulatory assessment answers a defined question
Use crop reports as context, with their uncertainty intact
Adoption needs an eligible population and an economic account

required_presentation_changes.prior: The CFIA plant-trait directive supplies environmental assessment criteria and applicant responsibilities. Its existence does not authorize an individual product, and an environmental decision does not establish food approval, seed distribution or profitable use. Readers should trace the specific product and jurisdiction through the relevant decision documents. This matters particularly when a research announcement describes a broad technology while the approval concerns a narrower trait or use. The report should explain that scope in ordinary language before discussing commercialization or regional implications.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained profile of CFIA Directive 94-08 describes environmental assessment criteria and applicant responsibilities for plants with novel traits. The directive itself does not authorize an individual plant, and environmental assessment does not establish separate food or feed approval, seed distribution or profitable use. A product claim needs its own identity, jurisdiction and applicable decision documents. A broad research technology and a narrower assessed trait or use must not be treated as the same scope. This editorial assessment reuses the dated profile; it does not newly verify later amendments, current legal authority or a product-specific approval.

claim_findings.section_heading: Separate a research program from a field result
claim_findings.rationale: Retain research awards and programs as funded questions, not successful traits or commercial adoption. Follow crop, trait, treatment, comparator, location, season and management through actual trials, including unsuccessful and inconclusive observations.

claim_findings.section_heading: Regulatory assessment answers a defined question
claim_findings.rationale: Qualify the paragraph as the retained Directive 94-08 profile and include feed as well as food approval. A generic directive or environmental assessment cannot establish a named product authorization, distribution or profitable use. This is an assessment of inherited framing, not new regulatory verification or legal advice.

claim_findings.section_heading: Use crop reports as context, with their uncertainty intact
claim_findings.rationale: Retain Crop Progress and WASDE as distinct aggregate reporting products, with issue dates, observation periods, geography, revisions and estimates/forecasts. Neither attributes one farm outcome to a particular technology or supplies an automatic final-harvest observation.

claim_findings.section_heading: Adoption needs an eligible population and an economic account
claim_findings.rationale: Retain actual seasonal use versus availability or interest, with farms, area and producers as separate adoption denominators. Costs, labor and access are analytical questions rather than established explanations; subgroup differences remain necessary.

Retain named trial and producer-cohort context, weather, irrigation, soils, management and measurement methods. Yield, water, resilience and income are separate outcomes; transfer beyond the observed setting is not assumed.

records.reviewer_kind: AI editorial assessment authorized by user
records.rationale: Accept the complete AI for Science chapter without further text changes. It treats methods, bounded pilots and institutional inventories as distinct from reproduced discovery or observed benefits. Its discussion of human responsibility concerns the external scientific workflow, not a human-signature prerequisite for this build.

readings.title: AI for Science: from model output to reproduced work

reviewed_section_hashes.heading: Locate the claim within the experiment
Evaluation resources are a starting point
Reproduction must include the surrounding workflow
Institutional use creates a second set of questions
Publish evidence that helps another researcher decide

claim_findings.section_heading: Locate the claim within the experiment
claim_findings.rationale: Retain the actual model contribution and different error consequences. Training, evaluation and new measurement data must remain distinguishable, with information exposure stated; the chapter does not claim to have run an experiment or established a discovery.

claim_findings.section_heading: Evaluation resources are a starting point
claim_findings.rationale: Retain NIST methods and TEVV resources as resources rather than endorsements. ARIA pilot scope, tested versions, participants and conditions do not establish general safety, fitness or transfer to a named scientific workflow.

claim_findings.section_heading: Reproduction must include the surrounding workflow
claim_findings.rationale: Retain versioned data, preprocessing, configuration, procedures, instruments, expert choices and failed-run exclusions. Computational reproduction and independent physical or biological confirmation answer different claims; no actual replication is invented.

claim_findings.section_heading: Institutional use creates a second set of questions
claim_findings.rationale: Retain NASA inventory-style institutional reporting without inferring accuracy, availability, cost or mission benefit. The proposed authorization, monitoring, suspension and human responsibilities concern the institution operating the scientific workflow; they do not impose a new human-review gate on the user-authorized AI editorial decision.

claim_findings.section_heading: Publish evidence that helps another researcher decide
claim_findings.rationale: Retain baseline workflow, AI contribution, inspectable experiment and bounded reproduction as separate evidence steps. Time, cost and scientific quality remain separate measures, and describing a limited demonstration is not a claim of general productivity or discovery benefit.
